title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry signed a two-year extension with the Patriots worth up to $20 million.
The extension includes $14.5 million guaranteed and a $4.2 million signing bonus.
Henry joined the Patriots as a free agent in 2021 and has made 259 catches and 26 touchdowns.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman crashed her 2011 Jaguar into a CVS in Acton, Massachusetts, causing significant damage.
Both the driver and her 88-year-old passenger from Acton were unharmed, as were all store employees and shoppers.
Acton Police requested a license suspension for the driver; the CVS will remain closed for repairs after the crash.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport's Runway 27 will close for 75 days starting August 31 for safety upgrades.
The closure will reduce runway capacity, potentially causing flight delays, especially in poor weather.
Nearby communities may experience increased air traffic and hear construction noise during the project.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on crash in Sandwich, Massachusetts, on Sunday night left one person dead and three injured.
The incident occurred around 8:50 p.m. near 87 Farmersville Road, involving a Toyota Prius and a Toyota RAV4.
The Prius driver died after being critically injured; RAV4 passengers sustained nonlife-threatening injuries, all treated at Cape Cod Hospital.

title: Driver on South Shore narrowly escaped before commuter train totaled his Camry
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 33-year-old driver mistakenly turned onto railroad tracks and exited his car before it was hit by a train.
The crash happened at 12:23 a.m. Sunday on the Greenbush Line near North Main Street in Cohasset.
The totaled 2016 Toyota Camry was removed from tracks, and North Main Street was closed for over two hours.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with psychiatrist under cross-examination
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Dr. Jennifer Tufts testified Lindsay Clancy denied having suicidal or homicidal thoughts before killing her children and attempting suicide.
Clancy's defense argues postpartum mental illness and psychiatric medications contributed to her actions, using an insanity plea.
Tufts initially diagnosed Clancy with anxiety and adjustment disorders, later considering but not diagnosing bipolar disorder.

title: For $415k, you can live in a New England community library
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: The Tyler Free Library in Foster, R.I., built in 1850, is listed for sale at $415,000.
The property, originally a schoolhouse, spans 1,760 square feet and sits on one acre.
The building retains library features like bookcases, but books will transfer to the Foster Public Library.

title: Patriots 53-man roster projection 1.0: Will New England really stick with 7 receivers?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots' 53-man roster includes Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito, and Behren Morton at quarterback, avoiding waivers for Morton.
Kayshon Boutte's position is uncertain as Patriots' receiver room remains crowded; trade could reduce receivers from seven.
Defensive depth concerns arise with Morgan Moses' age and Landry's health, leading to focus on young edge rushers like Gabe Jacas.

title: Adley Rutschman could make his Red Sox debut in coming days
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman, acquired on August 3, could debut for the Red Sox during their series with the Blue Jays in Toronto.
Rutschman has been sidelined since mid-July due to wrist inflammation but played two rehab games with Triple-A Worcester.
Boston Red Sox face roster decisions as Rutschman prepares to join, possibly impacting current catchers Connor Wong and Jake Rogers.

title: Healey signs bill allowing state to take Norwood Hospital through eminent domain
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Governor Maura Healey signed a bill allowing the state to seize Norwood Hospital through eminent domain starting November 1.
The law permits the state to transfer or lease the hospital property to a nonprofit for healthcare facility development.
Norwood Hospital has been inactive since a 2020 flood; prior construction halted due to Steward Health Care's bankruptcy.
